messages:
Anika Rao: Quick sync on authz cache. Seeing p50 policy eval 60-120ms on hot routes. Need ideas for sharding and invalidation that balance perf + correctness.

Tomás Rivera: Two options: 1) local gateway LRU cache keyed by (org,project,subject,action) for decisions, 2) compiled-policy cache (IR) to speed evals. Tradeoff is staleness when bindings change.

Priya Singh: Suggest TTL classes: admin-change TTL=0 + immediate push invalidate, default TTL=30s, low-risk TTL=5m. Admin revokes must take effect fast.

Dmitri Volkov: For push invalidation use NATS topic authz.invalidate.<org>. Gateways subscribe. But handle missed messages: TTL fallback. Include policy_version in invalidation payload.

Anika Rao: Agree. Add versioning to detect out-of-order invalidations. Also record invalidation correlation id for audit.

Tomás Rivera: Memory concern on gateways — shard by org hash and limit per-shard entries. Alternative: a policy-cache sidecar with durable store and ordered invalidation via streams. Sidecar isolates memory but adds ops complexity.

Priya Singh: Prototype both: gateway LRU + NATS invalidation (fast, simple) and sidecar + durable pubsub (robust). E2E tests must assert revoked role denies within 500ms in canary.

Dmitri Volkov: Metrics: invalidation_ack_rate, invalidation_lag, cache_hit_rate per-tenant. Runbook: if invalidation_lag >1s spike -> throttle admin writes and investigate broker.

sre-bot: Maintenance notice: nats-cluster maintenance 2026-04-02T01:00 UTC; expect short message loss window.

Anika Rao: Actions: Tomas prototype gateway cache (owner: Tomás), Dmitri prototype sidecar, Priya owns e2e/chaos tests, Anika builds dashboards + runbook. Will link RFC follow-up. Closing thread.
